check_sustainability.description: Check a list of seafood against FishWatch at once, such as the fish on a menu or an order from a supplier. Each species comes back with FishWatch's verdict on it, whether any of its stocks is overfished or being overfished, its bycatch and habitat impact, how it is farmed if it is, and any endangered species listing. The species with a stock in trouble are named in their own list, and a summary line says what was found. A name FishWatch does not cover is reported rather than stopping the step.

notFound.reason: FishWatch has no seafood profile for 'tilapia'. FishWatch covers about 120 species caught or farmed in US federal waters. A species fished mostly in state waters, a freshwater one or an imported one is not in it. List seafood profiles shows every species it has.

species.bycatch: Regulations and the use of modified fishing gear reduce bycatch.
species.habitatImpacts: Area closures and gear restrictions protect habitat that are affected by some kinds of trawl gear.
species.name: Atlantic Cod
species.population: The Gulf of Maine and Georges Bank stocks are overfished, but the fishing rate established under rebuilding plans promotes population growth.

stockAssessments.status: The Georges Bank stock is overfished and subject to overfishing (2021 stock assessment).

species.sustainability: Although populations are well below target levels, U.S. wild-caught Atlantic cod is still a smart seafood choice because it is sustainably managed under a rebuilding plan that allows limited harvest by U.S. fishermen.

A summary line names the leaders. NOAA lists a few species per 4 oz serving, which are scaled to 100 g, and says so.

get_seafood_profile.description: Read everything FishWatch says about one kind of seafood: whether it is a sustainable choice and why, whether its stocks are overfished or being overfished (in NOAA's words and as a plain Yes or No), how it is caught or farmed and what that does to habitat and bycatch, where it comes from and when it is in season, its taste, texture and color, and its nutrition facts as numbers. Also its Latin name, the names it is sold under, each stock's latest assessment, any endangered species listing, and an illustration.

about.appearance: Red snapper in deeper waters tend to be redder than those caught in shallower waters.
about.biology: Red snapper grow at a moderate rate, and may reach 40 inches long and 50 pounds.
about.habitat:
Larval red snapper swim freely within the water column.
Juveniles live in shallow waters over sandy or muddy bottom habitat.
about.introduction: U.S. wild-caught red snapper is a smart seafood choice because it is sustainably managed under rebuilding plans that allow limited harvest by U.S. fishermen.
about.range:
Red snapper are generally found at 30 to 620 feet deep in the Gulf of America and along the eastern coasts of North America, Central America, and northern South America.
They are rare north of the Carolinas.

mock_response.availability: U.S. wild-caught red snapper is available fresh year-round.
mock_response.bycatch: Regulations require modified fishing gear to reduce bycatch. Release techniques improve the chance of survival of unintentionally caught fish.
mock_response.color: The meat is pinkish with yellow tones when raw and turns somewhat lighter when cooked.
mock_response.fishingRate: The stocks are not subject to overfishing.
mock_response.habitatImpacts: Fishing gear used to harvest red snapper has minimal impacts on habitat.
mock_response.healthBenefits: Red snapper is low in saturated fat and sodium and is a very good source of protein.

mock_response.name: Red Snapper
mock_response.population: The Gulf of America* (formerly Gulf of Mexico) and South Atlantic stocks are not overfished.
mock_response.source: U.S. wild-caught from North Carolina to Texas.
mock_response.sustainability: U.S. wild-caught red snapper is a smart seafood choice because it is sustainably managed under rebuilding plans that allow limited harvest by U.S. fishermen.
mock_response.taste: Red snapper has a sweetly mild but distinctive flavor.
mock_response.texture: Red snapper is semi-firm, lean, and moist.

wildCaught.fisheryManagement: NOAA Fisheries with the Gulf and South Atlantic Fishery Management Councils manage red snapper in the United States.

In 2024, commercial landings of red snapper totaled approximately 8 million pounds and were valued at $43 million, according to the NOAA Fisheries commercial fishing landings database.
wildCaught.populationStatus:
There are two stocks of red snapper: The Gulf of America stock and the South Atlantic stock. According to the most recent stock assessments:
The South Atlantic stock is not overfished and not subject to overfishing (2024 stock assessment).

list_seafood_profiles.description: List the seafood FishWatch profiles: the species caught or farmed in US federal waters, about 120 of them. Narrow the list by name, by wild-caught or farmed, by kind (fish, shellfish, crab, shrimp, squid or seaweed) or by NOAA Fisheries region. Each comes back with its name, its profile's address, an illustration and the id every other action accepts, so a later step can look each one up.

description: Look up US seafood in NOAA FishWatch, the federal government's guide to sustainable seafood: about 120 species caught or farmed in US federal waters, from Alaska pollock to Gulf shrimp. For any of them, get FishWatch's answer to whether it is a sustainable choice, whether its stocks are overfished or being overfished, how it is caught or farmed and what that does to habitat and bycatch, where it comes from and when it is in season, what it tastes like, and its nutrition facts. Check a whole menu or supplier order at once, compare species' nutrition per 100 g, or list the profiles by region, kind or whether they are farmed. No account or API key required.
